title: Mitigate Helm upgrade-induced tenant KV drift with safe freeze and livepatch runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers running private/VPC on-prem clusters have reported upgrade failures during Helm-driven operator upgrades where tenant KV state diverges mid-migration. This ticket defines a mitigation strategy we call 'entropy attenuation' (controlled freeze + livepatch) and a runbook to safely quiesce affected tenants, apply a surgical KV rollback heuristic, and emit telemetry to prevent recurrence.

Background: During operator helm upgrades, we observed a race between the operator CRD migration job and tenant nodeagents applying small, conflicting writes to the on-disk KV (tenant-level manifest store). In high-churn environments this manifests as a partial schema bump that leaves tenants in a mixed-version state causing requests to 503 or enter reconcile loops. Existing hotfixes focused on broad rollbacks which risked data loss for tenants with partial writes. We need a more conservative automated approach that minimizes customer impact while restoring operator control.

Goals:
- Provide an automated 'tenant freeze' path that puts affected tenants into read-only mode quickly.
- Implement an idempotent KV-consistency-checker + rollback heuristic that prefers safety (preserve newer writes when safe) and can be run live with minimal downtime.
- Add operator-side coordination to delay CRD finalization until the heuristic completes for quarantined tenants.
- Ship a runbook and customer communication template for Solutions and Support.

Proposed approach:
1) Detect: add telemetry to operator pre-upgrade hook to compute a lightweight KV checksum fingerprint per-tenant and upload to upgrade-controller. If mismatch seen post-upgrade, mark tenant as QUARANTINED.
2) Attenuate (freeze): operator applies a tenant annotation that flips nodeagent and API proxies to read-only / maintenance mode. Expose a fast API to toggle this state.
3) Heal (livepatch heuristic): run a three-step safe-rollback:
   a) Snapshot current KV and S3/etcd backups (existing backup flow).
   b) Run merger heuristic that compares pre-upgrade and post-upgrade fingerprints, identifies keys with divergent schema markers, and either: prefer newer writes if they have intact schema markers, or fallback to pre-upgrade snapshot for keys with clear corruption.
   c) Apply fixes in a transactional manner with operator fencing to prevent concurrent writes.
4) Verify: run smoke tests and tokenized healthchecks and only unfreeze tenant after passing validation and remaining idle window.
5) Observability: emit events for each stage and surface in Console tenant page (quarantine state, repair progress, expected ETA).

Runbook attachments: see links for draft remediation script, Grafana dashboard, and a customer-facing email template.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Freezing tenants can disrupt customer SLAs; must be accompanied by timely ETA and status page updates.
- Heuristic errors could either preserve corrupted state or undo valid writes; we mitigate with mandatory snapshots and staged rollforward with operator gating.
- Adding pre/post fingerprinting increases pre-upgrade latency slightly; we will make it opt-in for Dedicated/Private clusters initially.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated detection of KV-fingerprint mismatch within 30s of operator rollout completion.
- Runbook can restore a quarantined tenant to a healthy state within 15 minutes in 80% of tested scenarios in our chaos lab.
- Console shows tenant quarantine state and repair progress.
- Support and Solutions team have communication templates and a triage checklist.
